lots.what_it_is: Three framed pictures: (1) genuine George Baxter senior oil colour print 'The Holy Family' (after Raphael's Madonna della Seggiola) on the title page of W. H. Callcott's 'Admired Sacred Melodies by the Most Celebrated Composers', mid 19th century, toned and stained, in a modern maple-look frame; (2) small hobby oil of a slab hut with ringbarked trees, signed 'H. Eyles'; (3) unsigned glazed pastel of a bushman on logs by a hut.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop of photo 4 reads 'PRINTED BY G. BAXTER, THE INVENTOR & PATENTEE OF OIL COLOUR PRINTING' under the image, then 'Admired Sacred Melodies, by THE MOST CELEBRATED COMPOSERS, Arranged for THE PIANO FORTE AS SOLOS AND DUETS ... BY [W. H.] CALLCOTT'; title 'THE HOLY FAMILY' at top. That one-line imprint is the Baxter senior form, consistent with the researcher. Publisher imprint at foot not visible. Photo 3 shows a cursive 'H Eyles' in cream paint on a canvas-board texture in an oak and gilt slip frame. Photo 5 pastel unsigned in visible area, reflections on glass.
lots.condition: Title page toned with foxing, brown stain top left and a horizontal crease; behind glass. Oil sound in photos. Pastel behind glass, condition of paper unseen.
lots.score_reason: A genuine but common Baxter music cover in tired condition (Baxter sold over 700,000 Holy Family impressions) plus a hobby oil and an amateur pastel. Tasmanian results for framed trios run $2 to $55 hammer, a single H. Eyles made $30, and a mounted Baxter Holy Family made $60 (2014). Likely whole-lot value $30 to $80.

lots.what_it_is: Venetian-style (Murano-type) caged pendant lantern: pale pink optic diamond-moulded blown glass held by brass wire ribs meeting at a point, cluster of cranberry glass knops at the top, brass ring, white flex and ceramic ceiling cup, about 28 cm. Unmarked; probably Italian later 20th century.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Glass is clearly blown into the wire cage (bulges between ribs), optic diamond pattern, cranberry-tinted knops at the top. No signature, label or sticker visible; only the house tag S178/4. The dark purple patch on the front reads as a reflection or seen-through knop, not an applied leaf. White ceramic ceiling cup and cord look modern.
lots.condition: No chips or cracks visible in the one photo; base point and rear unseen. Wire cage shows some tarnish. Electrics untested and wiring may need replacing for Australian compliance.
lots.score_reason: Attractive, decorative pink Venetian cage lantern. Close auction comparables sell for about AUD 60 to 115 hammer overseas, and Hobart glass pendant and Murano lighting make $90 to $200 hammer; dealer asks are much higher but optimistic. Realistic market about $80 to $150.

lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD in similar condition within 24 months is the Crafoord late 20th century Venetian lantern, USD 41 = AUD 58.9 (Mar 2025). 58.9 / 1.22 = 48.3, rounded down to $45 (all-in $54.90). Selling through a local auction at about 15% seller commission, no postage (glass is risky to post): 100 x 0.85 = 85. 85 / 2.44 = 34.8, rounded down to $30.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification of type with several close SOLD results whose pages I opened, but the piece is unmarked (no maker to read), the comparables are overseas and not identical in colour or cage, and there is one photo only with untested electrics.

lots.question_for_armitage: Any chips, cracks or repairs to the glass, especially at the pointed base and around the top knops? Is there any sticker or acid mark (Murano, Made in Italy)? Has the wiring been tested, and does the ceiling cup and flex come with it?

lots.what_it_is: Mixed lot: five 1940s Australian Army publications in their original card postal boxes (Khaki and Green, Stand Easy, Jungle Warfare, Active Service, and Soldiering On in red cloth), a worn 'New Guinea Victory' booklet, and a Don McLean 'Live in Concert' tour poster (John L Hansen Event Entertainment Presentation) with a pen signature.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 shows the boxed titles with paper address labels still on the boxes, Soldiering On in red cloth, New Guinea Victory with torn lower corner. Photo 2 shows a black pen signature reading as 'Don McLean' on the white strip below the image; no inscription, date or COA visible. Poster is glossy and appears rolled or folded, with some creasing.
lots.condition: Boxes scuffed and worn with old labels; books inside not seen, so contents and condition unknown. New Guinea Victory torn. Poster creased, signature unauthenticated.
lots.score_reason: The AMF/AWM books were printed in large numbers and sell for about $22 to $50 each retail; the boxed set adds a little appeal. The signed poster is the only upside, but Don McLean signed widely on Australian tours and there is no COA. Likely auction value $40 to $100 for the lot.
